# `Q-2-7` — Unclosed Single Quote

> A single-quoted construct opens with `'` but no closing `'`
> appears before the end of the block.

## What this means

Quarto markdown recognizes `'…'` as a typographic single-quote
pair (curly quotes in the output) when the quotes are balanced
within a block. This error fires when an opening `'` has no
matching close.

## Why this happens

The most common cause is an apostrophe being read as an opening
quote. A `'` directly after a word (`it's`, `the dogs' toys`,
`d'` before a code span) is always an apostrophe, but a `'` after
a closing delimiter such as `` ` ``, `**` or `_` (`` `a.rs`'s ``),
after whitespace, or at the start of a token is read as a quote
opener.

## How to fix

Add the closing `'`, or escape the literal apostrophe with a
backslash:

```markdown
He said it was \'just a draft\'.
```

If the construct really is a quote, supply the missing closing
mark.

## Example

A bare `'` with nothing after it triggers the error:

```markdown
'
```
